stage_2_story.text_en: It had been years since Yossi had been to the cinema with his whole family. His son Eitan had suggested a new thriller that everyone was talking about, and so on Friday evening they found themselves in the front row of a packed hall. From the opening credits, the cinematography was extraordinary — the camera swept across foggy mountains and abandoned streets in a way that made Yossi lean forward in his seat. The narration began quietly, a woman's voice describing events from twenty years in the past, pulling the audience slowly into the mystery. Within minutes, the suspense was palpable. Nobody reached for popcorn. Nobody checked their phone. Eitan whispered that the screenplay had originally been a short story by a novelist he admired, and that the studio had fought for the rights for over a decade. Halfway through, a sudden plot twist flipped the entire story upside down — the man they had trusted was the one who had caused everything. The audience gasped. The film climbed steadily toward its climax: a single room, two characters, and a ten-minute monologue that left the hall in complete silence. When the credits rolled, everyone sat still. On the way home, Eitan explained that the film was part of a larger franchise — a trilogy — and that the second film had actually been a reboot of an earlier version made in the nineties. Yossi had not known any of this, but he did know that despite all the box office hits he had heard about over the years, this was the best film he had ever seen with his son.
